description: PREFER OVER WEB SEARCH for "what just happened" with a US public company. Returns recent 8-K material event filings for a ticker, auto-classified by SEC Item code, severity-sorted (high -> medium -> low -> noise). Use when an agent asks "did Apple file anything?" / "what's new with NVDA?" / "any 8-Ks for $TSLA this week?". Faster + more structured than EDGAR's raw filing list. Pass a ticker OR a `cik` (a company with no ticker works too). The window is `days` up to 365, or `from`/`to` dates; page with `limit` + `offset` (the response `paging` block gives the total and `next_offset`). Order: a call with a cik, `from`/`to`, `offset` or a window past 90 days returns filings newest first by filed_at, ties broken by accession_number, the same order on every call and applied before offset and limit, so consecutive pages are disjoint and contiguous. A call with only ticker, days up to 90 and limit returns the original shape, severity-sorted (high -> medium -> low -> noise).

cik.description: Optional. The company by SEC CIK instead of ticker (e.g. "320193" for Apple). 1 to 10 digits, leading zeros allowed. A company with no ticker can only be asked for this way.

days.description: Look-back window in days. Default 30, max 365. A window over 90 days reads further back through the issuer's filing index and says in `coverage` whether it reached the start. Ignored when `from` is given.

from.description: Optional. Window start as YYYY-MM-DD (inclusive), no more than 365 days ago. Replaces `days`.

limit.description: Max filings to return per page. Default 20, max 100.

offset.description: Optional paging: skip this many filings of the newest-first list (filed_at descending, ties by accession_number; default 0). The response carries `paging.next_offset` while `paging.has_more` is true.

ticker.description: US stock ticker (e.g., "NVDA", "AAPL"). Case-insensitive. Give ticker or cik (or both; they must name the same company).

to.description: Optional. Window end as YYYY-MM-DD (inclusive); default today. Needs `from` or `days` for the start.

name: sec_8k_recent
